ip_top_stories.title: Sony Copyright Suit Survives AI Music Generator's Dismissal Bid
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has allowed Sony's copyright infringement lawsuit against an AI music generator to proceed, rejecting the defendant's motion to dismiss. The case is a significant development in ongoing litigation over AI-generated content and music copyright. This ruling keeps pressure on AI companies over their use of copyrighted material.

ip_top_stories.title: Copyright owners v AI developers: the emerging trends
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis of the evolving legal landscape between copyright owners and AI developers, examining emerging trends in how courts and legislators are handling these disputes. The piece covers key patterns in litigation and licensing negotiations across jurisdictions.

ip_top_stories.title: EU copyright law roundup – first trimester of 2026
ip_top_stories.summary: IPKat provides a comprehensive roundup of EU copyright law developments in the first three months of 2026, covering legislative and judicial activity relevant to AI and intellectual property. The summary covers key cases and policy developments across EU member states.

ip_top_stories.title: Monkey selfie from 15 years ago accidentally sets precedent for AI copyright dispute
ip_top_stories.summary: The landmark Naruto v. Slater monkey selfie case, which established that non-human authors cannot hold copyright, is now being cited as relevant precedent in AI copyright disputes. Legal commentators are examining how the ruling may shape courts' treatment of AI-generated works and ownership claims.

ip_top_stories.title: Is the government's stance on AI copyright holding back the UK tech scene?
ip_top_stories.summary: An examination of whether the UK government's current approach to AI and copyright — including its proposed text and data mining exceptions — is hampering the domestic technology sector. The piece weighs the interests of rights holders against those of AI developers in the context of UK policy.

ip_further_links.title: AI Music Generator Can't Duck DMCA Claim
ip_further_links.summary: A court has ruled that an AI music generator cannot avoid a DMCA copyright infringement claim, in a decision with implications for how digital music copyright law applies to AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: Analysing China's stricter examination standards for AI-related patent applications
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of China's tightened examination standards for AI-related patent applications and what this means for companies seeking IP protection for AI inventions.

ip_further_links.title: AI Makes Securing Copyright Protection for Software Code Tricky Guide
ip_further_links.summary: A guide examining the growing complexity of obtaining copyright protection for software code when AI tools are involved in its creation.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic Code Crisis Creates Copyright Contradiction
ip_further_links.summary: An examination of how Anthropic's practices around code generation are creating contradictions with copyright law, raising questions about ownership and liability for AI-produced software.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated content should be clearly labelled to help people spot fakes, committee says
ip_further_links.summary: A parliamentary or legislative committee has recommended that AI-generated content be clearly labelled to assist the public in identifying synthetic media, with implications for publishing and copyright policy.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns AI copyright when machines create art?
ip_further_links.summary: An overview of the unresolved legal question of who — if anyone — holds copyright over works produced autonomously by AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Don't believe the hype. Believe the data.
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines data-driven evidence on the actual impact of AI tools in the patent industry, cautioning against overstated claims about AI's transformative role in IP prosecution.

ip_further_links.title: Bologna Children's Book Fair 2026: AI Takes Center Stage
ip_further_links.summary: AI was a dominant topic at the 2026 Bologna Children's Book Fair, with publishers and industry figures debating its implications for children's publishing, rights, and creativity.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Exploring Data Spaces in Scholarly Communications
ip_further_links.summary: A Scholarly Kitchen guest post explores the concept of data spaces and their potential role in scholarly communications, with relevance to how research data is shared, licensed, and governed in an AI context.

ip_further_links.title: GitHub Policy Update
ip_further_links.summary: GitHub has issued a policy update with potential implications for how AI-generated and AI-assisted code is handled under its platform terms, relevant to software copyright questions.
